name: button
title: Button
description: The action a player takes that is not a choice: start, continue, play again, claim, share. Five treatments, which with the large size are the six the design draws: primary, secondary, tertiary for a dismissal that must not weigh as much as the thing it declines, destructive for an action that warns rather than invites, and icon for a square control holding one glyph and no words. Pressable controls move rather than fade, so the offset base collapses and the face lands where the base was. Disabled goes flat because it is never coming back; locked keeps its shape and shows a padlock because it is available later, and a player can tell those apart at a glance. Reads tokens only, so a theme change reaches it. Reports the press to the host; it does not start a round, claim a reward or share a result itself, and it does not fetch or settle anything. Use `choice` when the player is answering a question from presented options, and `selector` when they are picking one value from a set, such as a difficulty or a predicted goal total.
docs: Use variant="primary" for the one action on the surface, "secondary" for everything beside it, "tertiary" for a dismissal such as "Not now" or "Play as guest", and "destructive" for an action that warns, such as "Quit game". Use variant="icon" for a pause, mute or help control: its children are the glyph and it requires a `label`, because a glyph is a drawing and a drawing is not a name; the label lands in the accessible name as content rather than as aria-label, so the word "locked" still composes with it. Use size="large" for the hero action a player is meant to reach for. Pass `locked` when the action opens later and `disabled` when it never will. Locked refuses the click, including the one Enter and Space synthesise, but stays focusable so a screen reader can still describe it; disabled uses the native attribute and leaves the tab order.
